turns.text: Another cat's musk lies thick over the vent's warm grate, laid down within the hour — bold enough to sit right on top of last week's claim instead of skirting politely round it. That's not an accident. Ears track backward along the roofline before the rest of the body decides whether bold means trouble or just careless.

the vent breathes the same used-warm air it breathes every night, threaded up from the pod-stacks three floors below — rows of rented sleep racked floor to ceiling, each unit ticking a meter over whether the sleeper inside notices or not. the fresh scent belongs to a courier's tail, brushing past on a supply run two turns ago, not a challenge, just someone who didn't know this exact groove in the grating already belongs to somebody. overhead, a dish antenna angles a half-degree further down toward the stack, warming up on a schedule of its own.

Relief lands soft, almost too soft — the kind that a body already halfway back to dozing barely gets to feel before the eyelids start arguing with the discovery. No real threat, so no real reason to stay alert, and staying alert has never come easy up here anyway. Paws knead the grate twice, claiming the spot back the ordinary way, before the legs fold down on a schedule all their own.

the dish finishes its warm-up with a click that travels down through the grating itself, and three floors below a meter ticks over to a new hour without asking anyone's permission. something not-quite-sound slips up through the seams along with the warm air — a jingle, half-formed, tuna-bright, built for a sleeper's head and not for a cat merely lying near one. it arrives anyway. FRESH. DREAMS. RENTED. NIGHTLY.

Tuna-bright arrives as a taste before it arrives as anything else — phantom, metallic, blooming somewhere behind the tongue with no fish anywhere on this roofline to explain it. Head shakes once, hard, trying to shed a flavor that was never really in the mouth to begin with. Real smells push back — hot metal, old rain, a courier's fading trail — and mostly win.

the jingle thins as it filters grate to grate, losing shape the further it drifts from the dish, degrading into taste before it's gone completely. underneath it, closer, something else threads in: bitter solder, a junction box two vents over chewed open to bare copper by teeth with very particular opinions about where a building's signal ought to be spliced. whoever did that isn't here now. the smell is only a few hours old, and gnawed with more patience than hunger usually allows.

Solder-bitter pulls at the nose the way an open question always does — three steps taken toward it before the legs remember the dream-jingle hasn't finished dissolving yet, that this body is still half a beat behind itself tonight. Stops. Doesn't need somebody else's chewed wire on top of everything else. Turns back toward the warm grate, tail dragging with more reluctance than the decision deserves.

the courier doubles back along the same route, tail brushing the grate's edge a second time, close enough now to register as a shape instead of just a smell — thin, quick, unbothered, already gone again before any of it needs deciding. behind, the dish keeps humming its warm-up jingle down through the metal, patient the way rented things are patient when nobody's paying attention to stop them.

Nose meets nose for exactly as long as courtesy requires and not one breath longer — a check, not a greeting, confirming the shape matches the smell and the smell isn't looking for a fight. Ears stay half-back the whole time anyway. Old habit outlasts good information every time.

satisfied of nothing in particular, the courier peels off toward the far ledge and drops from sight, business elsewhere. two stories over, a different signal cuts in — dulcet, prettier, worse — an ad for the Compatibility Ward, promising a perfect match to anyone still awake to hear it, something about a refrigerator that remembers a birthday better than family does. it layers over the fading tuna jingle for three full seconds before both lose the fight to distance and fold back into ordinary rooftop static.

   ...picking through the neon rain...

None of it lands anywhere close enough to matter — not the fridge, not the birthday, not whatever debt a stranger's dream is quietly running up three floors down. Ears flick once at each, filed and dismissed in the same motion, fatigue winning ground it never had to fight hard for tonight.

past the dish, a billboard two blocks over cycles from a milk ad into something duller, an interest-rate notice nobody asked to see, then back to milk — the kind of loop that only the truly sleepless ever register as strange. the junction box two vents over stays quiet now, bled dry of whatever it was bled for. rain threatens without committing, the way it does most nights up here.

Claws rake the grate twice more, laying scent thick back over the courier's fading print, over the whole conversation this rooftop just had without asking for an opinion on any of it. Not anger. Just the shape maintenance takes when a body's too tired to make it mean more than upkeep.

the mark takes, the way marks always take on metal still faintly warm — good for another few days, maybe a week if the weather holds off. the dish eases back into standby, its half-degree tilt returning level, done feeding whatever sleeper below just got billed for another cycle of rented content. quiet settles back over the vent the way it settles every night, mostly.

Body folds down at last onto the reclaimed spot, warmth soaking up through fur faster than thought soaks out of it. The tuna-ghost is still there, faint, harmless now that it isn't fighting for control of anything. Eyes go to slits, then further.

the rooftop settles into its long stretch toward morning, the dish ticking through its schedule regardless of who's listening below, meters counting hours that get billed whether or not anyone's awake to notice them pass. the milk billboard keeps its loop going for no one. rain holds off, for now.

Last thought before the rest go quiet: the grate is warm, the print underneath is this cat's own again, and whatever's still bleeding faintly through the metal from three floors down isn't worth waking back up for. Paws tuck in. Tail wraps over nose.
sleep gets in anyway, uncharged, unmetered — the one thing tonight nobody up here figured out yet how to bill for.
